title: Instructions: the imperative (Lesen Sie! Lies!)
summary: Understand and give instructions, as teachers and bosses do: Lesen Sie bitte ..., Hör zu!, Kommt mal!
goals: Understand a teacher's instructions in class
Give polite instructions with Sie: Öffnen Sie bitte ...
Give instructions to a friend (du) or a group (ihr)

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 16: Sports and exercise (Ist das gesund?)

sections.title: The Sie form: verb first
sections.text:
The polite instruction is easy: the verb comes first, then [[Sie]]. [[Lesen Sie!]] = Read! [[Kommen Sie!]] = Come!

Add [[bitte]] to be polite: [[Lesen Sie bitte Seite zehn.]] It looks like a yes/no question, but the voice goes down at the end, and it ends with a full stop or an exclamation mark.

Separable verbs split as usual: [[Hören Sie zu!]] (zuhören) [[Kreuzen Sie an!]] (ankreuzen)

sections.title: The du and ihr forms
sections.text:
For **du**, take the du form, drop the -st and the [[du]]: [[du kommst]] becomes [[Komm!]], [[du machst]] becomes [[Mach!]], [[du hörst zu]] becomes [[Hör zu!]] After s or ß only the -t goes: [[du liest]], [[Lies!]]; [[du isst]], [[Iss!]]
- e→i and e→ie verbs keep the change: [[du nimmst]], [[Nimm!]]; [[Lies!]] and [[Iss!]] too
- a→ä verbs lose the umlaut: [[du fährst]], [[Fahr!]]; [[du schläfst]], [[Schlaf!]]
- [[sein]] is special: [[Sei pünktlich!]]

For **ihr** (two or more friends), use the ihr form without [[ihr]]: [[Kommt!]] [[Hört bitte zu!]] [[Seid leise!]]

Russian has a polite and an informal command too: Читайте! and Читай! German [[Lesen Sie!]] and [[Lies!]] work the same way. Armenian as well: կարդացե՛ք and կարդա՛. Читайте! and կարդացե՛ք are also the plural forms, so they cover German [[Lest!]] too.

sections.title: Make it softer
sections.text: A bare command can sound bossy. Add [[bitte]], and with friends also [[mal]] (just): [[Komm mal bitte!]] [[Öffne bitte das Fenster.]] [[Sag mal, ...]] = Tell me, ...

items.question: Which is the polite way to say 'Listen!'?
items.explanation: Sie form: Hören Sie zu! Hör zu! is for a friend, Hört zu! for a group of friends.
The verb first, then Sie. bitte can go after Sie, at the end or at the start.
